title: Stamp 1: Narrador and Voz Narrativa
welcome_lead: Stamp narrator and narrative voice in Spanish literary analysis.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on narrador, voz narrativa, and focalisation.

concepts.def: Narrator; the voice telling the story, distinct from the author.
Narrative voice; the manner in which the narrator presents the story.
Omniscient narrator with unlimited knowledge of all characters.
First-person narrator, often a character in the story.
Internal focalisation: events filtered through a character's consciousness.
External focalisation: only observable actions are described.

walkthroughs.body_html: The autor writes the text; the narrador tells the story. In Cien anos de soledad, the narrator is omniscient and intermittently magical, but not Garcia Marquez himself.
Camilo Jose Cela's La familia de Pascual Duarte (1942) uses a first-person criminal narrator. The reader sees only what Pascual chooses to share, raising questions of reliability.
If we share a character's thoughts, focalisation is internal. If only external behaviour is shown, external. If the narrator knows everything, zero focalisation (omniscient).
